key_insight: Accurate neural network approximation of the score function can be translated into a quantitative guarantee that the reverse diffusion model approximates the target data distribution in KL divergence, up to a terminal prior mismatch.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a principled error link between model capacity/score accuracy and generative fidelity, helping guide architecture and noise-schedule design for score-based diffusion systems.
method: Uses Hornik-style universal approximation theory to justify score-function approximation by neural networks.
Applies Girsanov’s theorem on path space to relate score error to distributional error in the reverse diffusion process.
Uses the data processing inequality for relative entropy to derive an explicit KL bound including noise schedule and terminal prior mismatch.
evidence_signal: The paper is theory-driven rather than empirical; it provides an explicit upper bound and proof-based guarantee instead of reporting experimental results.
watch_item: The bound is limited by the mismatch between the forward diffusion terminal distribution and the chosen reverse-process prior, which can leave irreducible approximation error.
paper_title: From Score Approximation to Distribution Approximation in Score-Based Diffusion Models
